profile.campus: Evocative South Bay / Silicon Valley cluster (with SJC14, SJC7)

source.basis: Operator facility page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

profile.address: 2151 Mission College Blvd, Santa Clara, CA 95054
profile.reading:
Per Evocative's own site, this Santa Clara, California facility, designated SJC11, sits at 2151 Mission College Boulevard and totals 73,000 square feet, drawing 9 megawatts of total power capacity delivered as two 4.5 megawatt feeds from diverse substations. Evocative describes the mechanical plant as two 1,200 ton Baltimore Air Coil cooling units backed by four 75 horsepower pumps, a five unit, 750 kVA UPS system arranged N plus 1, and four 1.5 megawatt Caterpillar generators for backup, and it markets the building as a Tier 3 design facility. The operator's own page states this building was originally an Intel network operations center and satellite facility that has since been completely updated for colocation use, and it puts roughly 11.9 million people within 100 miles of the site.

Evocative lists compliance with HIPAA, PCI DSS, SOC 2 Type II, SOC 3, ISAE 3402, SSAE 18, LEED, and Green Globes standards for this building, and names a broad carrier roster on site including AT&T, Lumen, Cogent, Comcast, Verizon, Zayo, Megaport, Bandwidth IG, Spectrum, and PacketFabric, alongside its own Evocative IP network and a listed interconnection to Silicon Valley Power, the municipal utility that also supplies the building's electric service. The company describes direct fiber connectivity to San Francisco in addition to that carrier list, and 24 hour access control, surveillance, and monitoring.

Evocative describes itself as a global infrastructure provider operating data center, bare metal, network, cloud, and managed services across 24 data centers in 14 metros, with this Santa Clara building one of two Evocative facilities in the South Bay alongside a separate SJC14 building elsewhere in the market. Santa Clara is headquarters to Intel Corporation and sits at the center of Silicon Valley's dense data center and technology corridor, alongside major colocation campuses operated by Equinix, Digital Realty, and CoreSite in the same city. The area draws power from Silicon Valley Power, the city owned municipal utility, and from Pacific Gas and Electric in surrounding areas, both interconnected to the CAISO grid that also serves much of central and northern California. Evocative has built part of its portfolio through acquisitions of smaller regional colocation operators, consolidating facilities like this former Intel site into a unified network under the Evocative name, a pattern consistent with the building's history as purpose built Intel infrastructure repurposed for third party colocation rather than constructed from the ground up as a commercial data center.

No tenant is named for this facility in any source reviewed, and no per rack or per square foot power density figure is published beyond the total 9 megawatt, dual 4.5 megawatt feed capacity described above.

reading.body:
The operator publishes 9 MW of total power capacity but no IT load figure, making it impossible to estimate this facility's AI hosting density or compare it to other compute sites by that metric alone.

SJC11 occupies 73,000 square feet of technical space split across two 4.5 MW feeds from separate substations. Floor area signals physical scale but does not determine capacity for AI workloads. Power density per square foot varies widely by facility design and tenant mix, so the square footage alone cannot tell whether this site hosts dense GPU clusters or sparse colocation racks. The dual-feed architecture suggests redundancy and resilience, which matters for uptime but not for the compute capacity question.

The six certifications, including SOC 2 Type 2, PCI DSS, and HIPAA, qualify the facility for regulated workloads in payments, healthcare, and financial services. They attest to audited controls and compliance infrastructure. None of them measure power density, cooling capacity, or suitability for the sustained high heat and electrical draw that GPU-scale AI training requires. Compliance and compute capability are orthogonal.

Among California's 103 mapped data center facilities in this dataset, only five publish a megawatt figure at all, totaling 170 MW. SJC11's published power places it in the sixth position statewide, but that ranking is nominal because it falls outside the five facilities that publish any power data. Within the Santa Clara County cluster, SJC11 is a mid-scale colocation asset whose relevance to AI infrastructure depends entirely on specifications the operator has chosen not to disclose.
